$comment: Phase-2 wave-1 OpenConnector ingestion config for BOAMP (Bulletin Officiel des Annonces des Marchés Publics), the French national procurement bulletin. Mirrors concurrentie-analyse/scripts/sync/sync_boamp_france.py's endpoint, selected fields and IT-descriptor filter. Public, unauthenticated OpenDataSoft Explore v2.1 API. Confirmed live 2026-07-05 with the script's own exact `select`/`where`/`order_by` shape (a real GET, not a POST body - simpler than TED/Belgium): the response is a flat `{"total_count": N, "results": [...]}` envelope (no `links`/`next` field - confirmed by inspecting the raw response - so OpenConnector's next-link pagination mode has nothing to attach to either), and one real record was captured and used to verify every mapped field path. The script's own `where` clause only ORs the FIRST 5 of its 10 IT_DESCRIPTORS codes (`IT_DESCRIPTORS[:5]` = 346/205/293/300/301) - this file bakes exactly that same 5-code OR clause as a static `query.where` value rather than all 10, to mirror the script's actual runtime behaviour, not an idealised version of it. IMPORTANT FIELD-SEMANTICS FINDING: BOAMP's own `descripteur_code`/`descripteur_libelle` fields (e.g. '346'/'Informatique') are BOAMP's internal classification thesaurus, NOT genuine EU CPV codes - the script's own comment says as much ('These map loosely to CPV 72xxx/48xxx'). Confirmed live by pulling this dataset's full field catalog (41 fields via GET .../catalog/datasets/boamp): there is no cpv-shaped field anywhere in it, only `code_departement`/`code_departement_prestation`/`descripteur_code`. Mapping the thesaurus codes into the spectr `tender.cpvCodes` field (which is documented as 'EU Common Procurement Vocabulary codes') would misrepresent non-CPV codes as CPV, so `cpvCodes` is deliberately left as a static empty array here, same treatment tenderned.json gives its own confirmed-absent case. `winner`/`titulaire` and `type_marche` beyond a single scalar have no home in the spectr `tender` schema (no 'winner' property exists on it at all) and are not force-mapped either. `nutsCode` mirrors the script's own `f"FR-{dept_str}"` construction (first element of the `code_departement` array, confirmed live to actually be an array e.g. `["21","25",...]` for multi-department notices, script itself only ever keeps the first). No sourceHashMapping - no spurious daily-recomputing field was found in the selected fields (unlike tenderned.json's aantalDagenTotSluitingsDatum case). KNOWN LIMITATION (pagination): the OpenDataSoft Explore v2.1 API paginates via `limit`/`offset` row-counts, not a page number, and (confirmed live) does not return a `links`/`next` field this connector could latch onto for OpenConnector's next-link pagination mode - the exact same class of mismatch as germany_bund.json's CKAN `start` param (OpenConnector's page-increment mechanism only ever sends a literal, incrementing page counter under a configurable parameter name, never a computed offset). `usesPagination` is therefore `false`, single call, `limit: 100` (matching the script's own PAGE_SIZE). LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-05 on the isolated spectr-spike instance: imported clean (4 objects), ran via POST /apps/openconnector/api/synchronizations/boamp-france-to-spectr-tender/run - `found: 100, created: 100`. Spot-checked several target objects field-by-field: sourceRef/title/organisation/publicationDate/procedure/typeOpdracht/nutsCode/tenderUrl all correct (including a real `closingDate` on a notice that has one, and a correctly-empty one on a notice that doesn't). Re-ran: `found: 100, updated: 100, created: 0` - same 100 target uuids reused, no duplicates. ONE READ-SIDE NUANCE FOUND while spot-checking `cpvCodes` (worth knowing, not a bug): the object API's JSON read representation OMITS the `cpvCodes` key entirely for these objects rather than showing `[]` - confirmed via a direct Postgres query against the magic table that the value IS genuinely and correctly stored as `'[]'::jsonb`, so this is a read-side 'omit empty arrays' presentation convention in OpenRegister's object-read serialization, not data loss - anyone spot-checking an intentionally-empty array/object mapping value against the generic object-read API should check the underlying storage (or a facet/aggregation query) rather than conclude the field is missing.

objects.name: BOAMP (Bulletin Officiel des Annonces des Marchés Publics)
objects.description: French national procurement bulletin, OpenDataSoft Explore v2.1 API. Public, unauthenticated, open license (1.6M+ total notices). Feeds the spectr `tender` register/schema via the boamp-france-to-spectr-tender synchronization, filtered to BOAMP's own IT-adjacent descriptor codes (see $comment for why these are NOT genuine CPV codes).

objects.name: BOAMP France to Spectr Tender
objects.description: Maps a raw BOAMP records-endpoint row onto the spectr `tender` schema. Mirrors the field selection of sync_boamp_france.py's per-row insert. All mapped field paths (id, idweb, objet, nomacheteur, dateparution, datelimitereponse, procedure_libelle, type_marche, code_departement, url_avis) confirmed live against a real records response on 2026-07-05.

objects.name: BOAMP France to Spectr Tender
objects.description: Wave-1 ingestion sync: BOAMP /records, filtered to the script's own first-5 IT descriptor codes (346/205/293/300/301), newest first -> spectr register, tender schema. `usesPagination: false` - OpenDataSoft's limit/offset paging is incompatible with OpenConnector's page-increment mechanism and the response carries no next-link (see $comment); `limit: 100` matches the script's own PAGE_SIZE.

query.where: descripteur_code LIKE '%346%' OR descripteur_code LIKE '%205%' OR descripteur_code LIKE '%293%' OR descripteur_code LIKE '%300%' OR descripteur_code LIKE '%301%'
